translations.literal: In the third year the sect rebels eyed Henan; Governor Wu Xiongguang garrisoned Lushi for defense, but many troops had been transferred elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year White Lotus rebels probed Henan; Governor Wu Xiongguang held Lushi, but most of his troops had been sent elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 寶豐、郟縣賊起，掠汝州。

translations.literal: Rebels rose in Baofeng and Jia County and plundered Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels rose in Baofeng and Jia counties and raided Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 布政使馬慧裕不嫺軍事，亮祿曰：「兵貴神速。

translations.literal: Provincial Commissioner Ma Huiyu was not skilled in military affairs; Liang Lu said, "In warfare speed is precious.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial Commissioner Ma Huiyu knew little of war; Liang Lu said, "In war, speed is everything.

sentences.zh: 今賊初起，烏合易滅，請兼程往剿。」

translations.literal: Now the rebels have just risen; this mob can easily be destroyed; I request to go by forced marches to suppress them."
translations.idiomatic: These rebels have only just gathered; a mob like this is easily crushed. Let me march at once to destroy them."

sentences.zh: 賊屯寶豐翟家集，東阻大溝，恃險不退，亮祿聲言京兵且至，樹八旗大纛，鞭馬腹，俾騰踔嘶號，聲震數里，賊懼；

translations.literal: The rebels encamped at Zhijiaji in Baofeng, blocked on the east by Dagou, relied on the perilous ground and would not retreat; Liang Lu proclaimed that capital troops were about to arrive, raised the great banners of the Eight Banners, whipped the horses' bellies to make them leap and neigh, the sound shaking for several li, and the rebels were afraid;
translations.idiomatic: The rebels held Zhijiaji in Baofeng, with Dagou blocking them on the east, and refused to retreat from the strong ground; Liang Lu announced that capital troops were coming, raised the great banners of the Eight Banners, and had his men whip their horses' flanks until they reared and neighed, the noise carrying for miles, terrifying the enemy;

sentences.zh: 夜吹角而進，躍馬逾壕，火其寨，一鼓殲之，擒其渠李岳等。

translations.literal: at night he blew horns and advanced, leaped his horse over the moat, set fire to their stockade, destroyed them in one assault, and captured their chiefs Li Yue and others.
translations.idiomatic: that night he sounded the horns and attacked, leaped the moat on horseback, burned their camp, wiped them out in a single assault, and captured their leaders, including Li Yue.

sentences.zh: 奏入，仁宗大悅，立擢副將。

translations.literal: When the memorial arrived, the Renzong Emperor was greatly pleased and immediately promoted him to deputy brigadier.
translations.idiomatic: When the report reached court, the Renzong Emperor was delighted and immediately promoted him to deputy brigadier.

sentences.zh: 累遷雲南開化鎮總兵。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Brigadier of Kaihua Town in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to brigadier of Kaihua in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 七年，卒，帝甚惜之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he died, and the Emperor deeply regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventh year, to the Emperor's deep regret.

sentences.zh: 論曰：恆瑞、慶成戮力襄陽，剿匪最久，後皆獨當一面，功過不掩，故仁宗始終保全。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Heng Rui and Qing Cheng exerted their strength together at Xiangyang and suppressed the bandits the longest; afterward each commanded a separate front; merits and faults did not cancel each other out; therefore the Renzong Emperor preserved them to the end.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: Heng Rui and Qing Cheng fought side by side at Xiangyang longer than any other commanders in the campaign; each later held an independent command; their merits and faults stood on their own record, and the Renzong Emperor stood by them to the end.

sentences.zh: 七十五孤軍苦戰，徒以失懽群帥，未奏顯功，論者惜之。

translations.literal: Qishiwu fought bitterly with an isolated army, but only because he lost the favor of the commanders in concert did he fail to achieve notable success; commentators regret this.
translations.idiomatic: Qishiwu fought heroically with isolated forces, but fell out with his fellow commanders and never won a decisive victory; later writers have mourned the waste of his talent.

sentences.zh: 富志那獨平枝江、宜都一路，移鎮苗疆，與傅鼐和衷弭亂，有足稱焉。

translations.literal: Fu Zhina alone pacified the route through Zhijiang and Yidu, transferred to garrison the Miao frontier, worked in harmony with Fu Nai to quell disorder, and has achievements worth praising.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zhina alone pacified the Zhijiang–Yidu corridor, then transferred to the Miao frontier, where he worked in concert with Fu Nai to end the unrest — a record well worth honoring.
